newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos sees fiscal surplus for year.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos sees fiscal surplus for year.

text.p: Venezuela will close the year with a fiscal surplus equivalent to one percent of gross domestic product (GDP), Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.

"We expect a fiscal surplus of around one percent of GDP ...(and) we continue to see four percent growth for 1997," Matos told reporters after speaking at a seminar that reviewed the first year of Venezuela's economic reform program.
Matos said certain lead indicators, such as car sales and construction, had already shown strong signs of recovery.
"Some analysts say growth will be above five percent," he added.
Venezuela's economy shrank 1.6 percent in 1996 when 4.9 percent growth in the oil sector failed to compensate for a 3.6 percent slip in the non-oil economy.
